extracted.intended_audience: writers submitting non-fiction (essays, interviews, roundtables, columns) to Strange Horizons
extracted.subtask_description: Guidelines for preparing and submitting non-fiction (critical/academic essays, interviews, roundtables, and columns) to the online magazine Strange Horizons, including required formats, lengths, editorial expectations, rights, and process. Targets pieces about speculative fiction, its history, theory, fandom, and related cultural topics.

rubrics_metrics.name: Original contribution to SF discussion
rubrics_metrics.description: Non-fiction published in Strange Horizons should provide an original contribution to the field's discussions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Articles should represent a substantial original contribution to SF discussion; browse the articles archive for examples. Editors encourage consideration of Strange Horizons' focus on marginalised traditions and voices.

rubrics_metrics.name: Welcoming marginalised and new voices
rubrics_metrics.description: Strange Horizons is interested in submissions from new and established writers, and in particular welcomes submissions from voices that have historically been marginalised within the SF community.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Authors should consider the publication's focus on marginalised traditions and voices when preparing submissions.

rubrics_metrics.name: No AI-generated submissions
rubrics_metrics.description: We will not accept any submissions generated by any form of genAI.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Any submission created by generative AI is disallowed. Do not submit AI-generated text.

rubrics_metrics.name: Essay length and topical scope
rubrics_metrics.description: Essays: short original critical and academic essays of 3,000 to 5,000 words about works of speculative fiction, SF history, associated SF theory and criticism, and SF fandom and culture.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Essays should be within the 3,000–5,000 word range and focussed on relevant SF topics; examples of published essays are linked in the guidelines.

rubrics_metrics.name: Essay scholarly awareness and argument
rubrics_metrics.description: Essays should be aware of previous writing in their area (popular and/or scholarly) and propose an original argument.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Demonstrate engagement with earlier work and make a clear, original argumentative contribution rather than merely summarising existing commentary.

rubrics_metrics.name: Essay citation and source presentation
rubrics_metrics.description: Essays should cite their sources using endnotes (with links to online sources where available). Works discussed may be listed in a bibliography.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use endnotes for citations and include links for online sources where possible; include a bibliography if appropriate. Note that some essays may be reviewed by external specialists.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reprints policy
rubrics_metrics.description: Strange Horizons occasionally reprints essays that represent significant contributions to SF criticism. Reprints are selected by the editors; please do not submit work for reprint consideration.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not submit previously published work for reprint consideration; reprints are chosen by editors and are not open to submission.

rubrics_metrics.name: Interview length, format, and metadata
rubrics_metrics.description: Interviews will typically be 3,000 to 5,000 words long and should be presented in a question-and-response format, with a short biographical and contextual introduction, including the date when the interview was conducted.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide a clear Q&A format plus a short introduction that includes interviewee bio/context and interview date. Aim for thoroughness appropriate to a knowledgeable reader.

rubrics_metrics.name: Interview tone and question quality
rubrics_metrics.description: Interviewers must be respectful, and should help interviewees to put forward their points in their most complete and thoughtful form. However, interviewers should not be deferential—an interview is not simply a platform for an individual to promote their work. Questions should be specific rather than generic, and interesting answers should be followed-up rather than left hanging.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Craft specific, probing questions and follow up on interesting responses. Maintain respectful but not promotional tone; enable depth for a knowledgeable readership.

rubrics_metrics.name: Roundtable length, participant count, and editorial standards
rubrics_metrics.description: Roundtable discussions should be 5,000 to 10,000 words involving between three and five informed commentators.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Roundtables are an opportunity to explore a subject from multiple perspectives. They should be carefully moderated and edited for flow; they should not simply be a chat transcript or pasted-together email discussion. Contributors should have the opportunity to ensure their arguments are worded as they wish.

rubrics_metrics.name: Roundtable moderation and anti-patterns
rubrics_metrics.description: Roundtables should be carefully moderated and edited for flow; they should not simply be a chat transcript or pasted-together email discussion.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Edit submissions so the discussion reads coherently; organise and moderate contributions rather than presenting raw transcripts or unedited email chains.

rubrics_metrics.name: Roundtable contributor approval
rubrics_metrics.description: Contributors should be given the opportunity to ensure they have put forward the best wording of their arguments.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide contributors the chance to review and approve wording to ensure accuracy and clarity of their contributions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Column length and audience level
rubrics_metrics.description: Columns are standalone personal essays of 1,000 to 2,000 words. When writing your column, assume an informed but non-specialist audience.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Keep columns within 1,000–2,000 words, write for informed general readers rather than specialists, and provide an argued point of view.

rubrics_metrics.name: Column content style
rubrics_metrics.description: Columns should provide an argued point of view. Convention or conference reports grounded in personal experience are welcome. However, journalistic summaries should be avoided.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Focus on opinion/analysis rather than news-reporting; personal, experience-grounded pieces are acceptable when they make an argument.

rubrics_metrics.name: Columns submissions: single pieces only
rubrics_metrics.description: We have a roster of regular columnists and are not looking for additional regular columnists at this time; please only submit for single pieces.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Submit columns as one-off pieces unless explicitly invited to join the roster of regular columnists.

rubrics_metrics.name: Submission file formats and formatting
rubrics_metrics.description: All submissions should be sent either as a rich text file (.rtf) or as plain text (ASCII) in the body of your email message. Submissions that are not properly formatted may not be read.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use .rtf attachments or plain ASCII email body text. Ensure clear formatting to avoid automatic rejection.

rubrics_metrics.name: How to query and what a query should include
rubrics_metrics.description: For essays, interviews and round-tables you may send queries first. Email queries to articles@strangehorizons.com with the subject heading [QUERY], followed by the type of piece you are querying for, and its working title. A query should outline your proposed piece, why it will be of interest to readers of Strange Horizons, and the time frame in which you would be able to complete it.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Queries should succinctly explain the piece, its reader interest, and completion timeframe. Use the specified subject header and email address.

rubrics_metrics.name: Where and how to submit completed pieces
rubrics_metrics.description: Completed feature non-fiction should be emailed to articles@strangehorizons.com with the subject heading [SUB] followed by the type of work you are submitting and its title. Columns should be emailed to columns@strangehorizons.com with the subject heading [SUB] followed by the title of the column.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Follow the exact subject-line conventions and email addresses for different piece types to ensure proper routing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Response time and follow-up policy
rubrics_metrics.description: For complete submissions, we should respond within 4 weeks. If you have not heard from us within this time, email articles@strangehorizons.com as appropriate, with the subject heading [FOLLOW-UP], followed by the title of your original submission. We will only respond to queries if they are of interest. If you have not had a response to your query within 4 weeks, you can assume that we are not interested.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Expect ~4 weeks for a reply; follow the follow-up subject header if necessary. Do not expect responses to queries unless the editors are interested.

rubrics_metrics.name: Payment rates
rubrics_metrics.description: We pay: $75 for a column; $40 for a reprinted essay; $150 for an original essay; $45 to an interviewer, and $45 to an interviewee; $20 to a roundtable moderator, and $20 to each other contributor.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These are the stated rates for accepted pieces and contributors; plan accordingly when proposing commissioned or unpaid work.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rights and post-publication display
rubrics_metrics.description: We acquire exclusive online publication rights for 6 months from the date of publication and request ongoing non-exclusive rights to display the work in our archive. At any point after 6 months following first publication, contributors have the right to request the removal of their material from our archive.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Accepted pieces grant Strange Horizons six months exclusive online rights, with ongoing non-exclusive archive display unless the contributor requests removal after six months.

rubrics_metrics.name: Editorial volunteer status / realistic expectations
rubrics_metrics.description: The articles editors are volunteers. Please bear in mind they also have lives outside of editorial duties.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Be patient and considerate with editors; factor volunteer response time into your planning.
